title: Introduce anchor-driven failure replay with progressive quarantine throttler
author: Ethan Park
ci_status: pass (pipeline retried after two flaky integration failures)
release_notes: Introduces an anchor-based failure replay component and a progressive quarantine throttler for eval CI: reduces noisy rollbacks by replaying anchored failures deterministically and throttling problematic prompt cohorts; adds a new CI job 'eval-anchor-replay' and observability tags for anchored replay runs.
description: Motivation: Spikes of noisy eval failures (often transient or infra-related) are triggering rollbacks and incorrect regression signals. This PR introduces an anchor-driven failure replay system that replays a small, provenance-anchored sample of failing requests against the candidate and baseline in isolation, plus a progressive quarantine throttler that limits the blast radius of cohorts that produce repeated non-deterministic failures. Key goals: reduce noisy CI failures, improve root-cause signal for real regressions, and keep reruns bounded and auditable. What this changes: 1) eval_harness/orchestrator/anchor_replay.py: new replay engine that captures request/response provenance and replays deterministically with KV-cache seeding; 2) ci/hooks/anchor_replay_hook.py: CI hook that marks failing eval jobs for anchored replay and triggers the replay job; 3) ci/configs/progressive_quarantine.yaml: tunable policy for tiered quarantine (soft hold -> partial throttle -> full quarantine) with exponential backoff and decay; 4) metrics: adds eval.anchor_replay.* tags, replay_outcome, quarantine_state and quarantine_duration to perf telemetry; 5) tests: integration and unit tests covering deterministic replay paths and quarantine transitions under simulated flakiness; 6) docs/ci/anchor-replay.md: operational runbook and troubleshooting. Backwards compatibility: the hook is opt-in by default for projects; existing eval pipelines are unchanged until the new ci job is enabled. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1987) - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Metrics and traces emitted - [x] Opt-in config and sane defaults - [x] Docs and runbook included How it works (brief): when an eval job fails, the hook attaches a compact anchor snapshot (seed prompt IDs + minimal context + tokenization fingerprints). The anchor-replay job takes those anchors, rehydrates deterministic inputs (fixing RNG seeds, KV cache priming) and runs the candidate and baseline in an isolated environment with strict timeouts and dual-run tracing. If a replay confirms a regression we escalate; if a replay is unstable (non-deterministic) we transition the cohort through the quarantine throttler which progressively reduces traffic routed to the cohort for live shadowing and increases sampling frequency for targeted repro attempts. Observability and safety: replay runs are tagged and stored, and the runbook documents triage steps to avoid accidental rollouts based solely on single-run failures. Performance considerations: replay is intentionally small (anchors limited by size and capped to N per job) to keep cost low; quarantine throttler uses exponential backoff to avoid constant reruns. Related work: builds on ideas in ENG-2042 (anchored probes) and the regression-blame tooling (prior PR).

review_comments: Leah Chen: Can the anchor snapshot be further size-bounded? I saw a case where context blowup could make anchors large. Suggest enforcing token limit and dropping large attachments.
Ethan Park: Good point — implemented a token cap and gzip-on-write for anchor payloads in commit d7c1b05. Updated docs to note the cap.
Marco Ruiz: Integration tests are flaky in CI (timeout on replay run). Please add a shorter timeout variant for CI to avoid long-stalled jobs.
Ethan Park: Added a CI-only timeout override and a debug flag to collect replay traces on timeout in f4126a0.
Priya Nair: How does quarantine interact with canary rollouts? We should avoid silently throttling a canary route.
Ethan Park: Quarantine is not applied to explicit canary routes by default; added an opt-in flag in the config and clarified in the runbook.
Marco Ruiz: Approve after CI re-run — last build had two flaky integration failures but core unit tests look good.
Leah Chen: Approving. Observability hooks look sufficient to triage future incidents.

notes_for_mergers: This change is opt-in. When enabling, monitor eval.anchor_replay.replay_outcome and quarantine_state metrics for three days. Engineering oncall: @marco_ruiz and @leah_chen.
